run_label: v10 c50 disambiguation eval — c50 has best eval_loss but least training

model.name: v10 c50 FP8
model.training: 50 steps, lora_rank=64, freeze_vit=false, v9b trajectory injected into prompts
model.selection_reason: lowest eval_loss among all v10 checkpoints; used as undertrain-disambiguation point

purpose: Disambiguate whether Run 85's v10 c150 (agg F1 0.329, 1 precision-clean new-venue goal) is undertrained or overtrained relative to the loss-curve sweet spot. c50 has lowest eval_loss but only 1/3 the trajectory exposure of c150. If c50 > c150 → c150 is overtrained → continue-train with longer warmup. If c50 < c150 → c150 is undertrained → eval c200 (run 93+).

run_83_phase2.partial: game_20 F1=0.289 (goal 1/9), game_22 F1=0.204 (goal 0/5); killed before game_21/rush

targets.success_criteria: new-venue goal recall > 4/16 OR aggregate F1 > 0.40
targets.iteration_signals: If any new-venue game produces a precision-1.0 goal detection (0 FP on goals), v10 is worth iterating on regardless of overall F1. FP8 quant noise is ~0.03 F1, so single-game F1 deltas of that size are within noise.
targets.decision_after_c50: If c50 agg F1 > c150 (0.329) AND new-venue goal calls increase, c50 wins → defer c200. If c50 worse, eval c200. If c50 same/marginal, eval c200 anyway to pick a definitive checkpoint.

hypothesis: v10 c150 was the empirical pick from a non-monotonic eval-loss curve. c50 (lowest loss) tests whether the language model has learned trajectory reasoning by step 50 — if yes, more trajectory exposure beyond c50 is wasted; if no, c50 will collapse on new venue goals (where c150 already barely produces).
next_run: TBD pending c50 eval result, then c200 eval (run 93-96)
